paite: Huchi in Job in adawng a, hichi in achi:
heading: Job Thugen Masa
english: Then Job answered,

paite: "Aw ka lungzinna kibuk thei hi henla, ka tuahsiatna selbukna ah kikoihkhawm thei hileh!
english: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

paite: Tu in tuipite a piaunel sang in agikzaw ding: huaiziak in ka thugente leng akhauh hi.
english: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore my words have been rash.

paite: Bangkim hihthei thalte lah ka sung ah a-om ngal a, agu uh huai a kipan a ka kha in adawnvek; kei dou ding in Pathian mulkimhuainate akivual uhi.
english: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

paite: "Anek ding loupa mu, gam sabiltung aham a hia? Ahihkeileh gan an mu bawngtal aham a hia?
english: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

paite: Chi tel lou in gim nei lou akine thei dia hia? Ahihkeileh aktuida ah limna mawngmawng a-om a hia?
english: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

paite: Ka kha in amaute akhoih nuam kei; kei a ding in an kihhuai bang ahi uhi.
english: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

paite: "Aw ka nget tang thei leng zaw; ka thil deih Pathian in hon phalleh zaw.
english: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

paite: Kei hon hihgawp ding in Pathian deihlam hi lai henla; akhut zan in, kei hon satkhe maileh.
english: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

paite: Huchi in lungmuanna ka nei lai dia; ahi, damlou natna ah ka kipak ding hi; Mi Siangthou thute ka kitheihmohbawl ngal kei a.
english: Let it still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

paite: Ka hatna bang ahia, ka ngak ding? Huan ka beina bang ahia, ka kuhkal ding?
english: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

paite: Ka hatna suangte hatna hi hia? Ahihkeileh ka sa dalsik hia?
english: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?

paite: Kei ah panpihna a-om het kei a, kei a kipan theihsiamna hawlmang in.
english: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, that wisdom is driven away from me?

paite: "Bah dia mansa a om kiang ah alawm in siamna a-etsak ding ahi kei maw; huchi lou in Bangkim hihthei kihtakna tawpsan ahi kei ding maw.
english: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

paite: Luita bang in ka unaute alepchiah uh; luita mangthang luanna bang in.
english: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

paite: Huai tui khal ziak a vom a; huai a vukkhal akisel.
english: which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

paite: Alum hun chiang in atuimang ua, asat chiang in amun ua kipan amangthang uhi.
english: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

paite: Huai lampi a khualzinte a pial ua, bangmah omlouhna mun ah apaitou ua, amangthang uh.
english: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.

paite: Tema khualzinte'n azong ua, Sheba pawlte'n alamen uh.
english: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

paite: Akilamet hang un azahlak uh; huai lam ah ava pai ua azahlak uh.
english: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

paite: Tu in bangmah na hi ngal kei ua; mulkimhuaina na mu ua, na lau uhi.
english: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

paite: Kei hon pia un? Ahihkeileh na neih-le-lam ua kipan in kei a ding in thilpiak lan un, ka chi hia?
english: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?

paite: Ahihkeileh, melma khut a pan hon tan un, mihat khut a pan hon hukhia un ka chi hia?
english: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?

paite: "Hon sinsak in, huan ka dai ding: ka diklouhna hon theisiamsak un.
english: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.

paite: Thudikna thute hat hi nah e: himahleh miselna in bang aselphou a?
english: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

paite: Thute selphou ding a um na hi uhia? Chimoh mi thugente huih bang ahi chih thei in.
english: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

paite: Ahi, pa neiloute tung ah ai na san ua, na lawm uh sumsinna van in na bawl uh.
english: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

paite: Tu in hehpih in hon en un; na ma uah thuzuau ka gen kei a.
english: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.

paite: Kik nawn un ka hon ngen ahi, diklouhna om kei hen; ahi, kik nawn un, ka thu adik ahi.
english: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

paite: Ka lei ah diklouhna a-om hia? Ka lei in thil hoih lou atheikak thei kei dia hia?"
english: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
